$comment: Public repositories used to measure the product on real code.
Each entry is pinned to a commit SHA so the measurement is reproducible:
a moving target would make every benchmark run incomparable with the last,
which is the same mistake as measuring against a moving specifier. Bump a
SHA deliberately, in its own change, so a metric movement can be attributed
to the repository rather than to us.
Selection criteria, in priority order:
- TypeScript or JavaScript source, since those are the languages the
analyzer supports; a Python repository would measure nothing.
- Chosen for the syntax it contains, not for how well known it is. A
repository picked for its popularity measures the syntax its maintainers
happened to use, which is how an entire language feature (TSX) went
unexercised across eight well-chosen repositories.
- Permissively licensed, so the benchmark is unambiguous about what it is
doing with the code. Nothing is vendored: each repository is cloned into a
temporary directory, measured, and deleted.
- A spread of sizes and shapes, so the token-budget buckets and the module
detection are exercised on more than one kind of layout.
- Small enough to clone quickly. The point is many repositories measured
often, not one large one measured rarely.
Run with: npm run benchmark:public
On CI it runs on a schedule and on demand, so a network-dependent job cannot
block a pull request.

repositories.name: clsx
repositories.note: Tiny single-file TypeScript package: the lower bound of the size range.

repositories.name: p-map
repositories.note: Small TypeScript package with several runtime dependencies.

repositories.name: ansi-styles
repositories.note: Older CommonJS codebase, to check the analyzer does not assume modern module syntax.

repositories.name: ky
repositories.note: Modern ESM TypeScript with tests colocated next to sources.

repositories.name: ora
repositories.note: TypeScript with build output committed and a wider dependency surface.

repositories.name: execa
repositories.note: Larger modern TypeScript package: exercises the 8-64 KB size bucket.

repositories.name: got
repositories.note: Substantial TypeScript package with deep internal directories.

repositories.name: changesets
repositories.note: npm workspaces monorepo, so cross-package resolution is measured on something other than our own layout.

repositories.name: radix-primitives
repositories.note: TSX at scale, and a pnpm workspace with dozens of packages importing each other by subpath. Chosen for the syntax it contains rather than its popularity: it is the repository that found the JSX gaps.
